Sed inprimis Diuina hinc eminet gloria, quæ in pœnis improborum, & excidio perditorum æque emicat, atque in præmiis fidelium, & sanctorum honore; neque minime etiam in eo est conspicua, quod mortalium omnium omnes actiones, in bonum possit conuertere, & ex malitia aliorum depravata, non modo sui nominis celebritatem, sartam-tectam conseruare, sed & miris modis adaugere. Recte Clemens Alexandrinus: {q}Diuina sapientia, & virtutis, & potentia est officium, non solum bona facere (hæc est enim, ut semel dicam, Dei natura, ut ignis calefacere, & lucis illuminare) sed illud quoq; maxime, ut id, quod per malos aliquos excogitatum est, ad bonum aliquem finem, & vtilem deducat, & vtiliter iis, quæ viden-turtur mala, vtatur. Permittit ergo mala, qui non facit mala. Et, qui ex praeceptis legis, peccata iaterdicit, à nequitia deterrens; tolerat tamen fieri. Vbi illud Augustini veritatem obtinet: r Propterea magna opera Domini, exquisita in omnes voluntates eius, vt miro & ineffabili modo, non fiat praeter eius voluntatem, quod etiam contra eius fit voluntatem, quia non fieret, si non fieret, nec vtique nolens finit, sed volens.
units.tr: Augustine, against Faustus the Manichaean, book 21; and On Heresies, to Quodvultdeus, heresy 66 (Epiphanius). He who stores up tears in a bottle (cf. Ps. 56), who observes the sparrows falling to the ground, who is known to count the hairs of the head, knows perfectly all the deeds of creatures. Nothing therefore happens without his knowledge, let alone against his will, or in spite of his efforts to prevent it. He dissolves the daring and the attempts of the most powerful, according to his good pleasure. If he holds Satan himself in chains, how much more will he restrain his ministers and clients? They cannot rage with greater savagery or fiercer fury than the Governor of all things has deemed fit. The Jews, Haman wished to root out utterly; the forty conspirators desired to kill Paul, but God prevented it. Nor will other wickednesses of the ungodly be carried out, unless God permits it. Thus the errors and sins of the regenerate and the elect come about with his permission. He who restrained David from the bloodshed of Nabal, which he had sworn, could also have called him back from the murder of Uriah and from the crime of adultery. He who foretold to Peter the denial of his Master (Matt. 26) could also have prevented it and altogether hindered him from denying. But God allows men to persevere in the purpose of their hearts: partly so that the condemnation of the reprobate may be more just; partly so that the elect, humbled by the consideration of their own falls, may conduct themselves more cautiously in future. But above all, the divine glory shines forth here, which shines equally in the punishments of the wicked and the destruction of the lost, as in the rewards of the faithful and the honour of the saints; and not least is it conspicuous in this, that he can turn all the actions of all mortals to good, and, from the depraved malice of others, preserve not only the fame of his name whole and unharmed, but even increase it in wondrous ways. Clement of Alexandria rightly says: The wisdom, virtue and power of God have this task: not only to do good (for this, to say it once, is the nature of God, as it is of fire to heat and of light to illuminate), but above all to lead what has been devised through some wicked persons to some good and useful end, and to use in a useful way those things which seem to be evil. He therefore permits evils, who does not do evils; and he who, by the precepts of the law, forbids sins, deterring from wickedness, nevertheless tolerates that they be done. Here Augustine's truth holds: Therefore the great works of the Lord, sought out in all his wills, so that in a wondrous and ineffable manner nothing is done outside his will, which is done even against his will, since it would not be done if he were not willing it, and assuredly he does not permit it unwillingly, but willingly.

units.la: 6. Tertio, immortalis Deus, proæterni sui decreti ratione, quemadmodum aliquibus, apprehensionem coelestium, fidemque subministrat, sic, aliis, quos in æternas præconstituit flammas, subducit gratiam; qua qui semel deserti tuuntur, in omne nefas, sine modo, aut mensura proruunt.
units.tr: 6. Thirdly, the immortal God, by the reason of his eternal decree, just as he supplies to some the apprehension of heavenly things and faith, so from others, whom he has preordained to eternal flames, he withdraws grace; and those who, once abandoned by it, are carried headlong into every wickedness without limit or measure.

units.la: Apostolus / sæpe, iis ad quos scribit: Priusquam cordibus vestris illuxisset Christus, fuistis Gentiles; sine Deo in hoc mundo; fœditate conspurcati; nequitia obducti. Et quotquot sint, quibus non præfulget Spiritus; in nihil non malorum feruntur præcipites. Non ad terram magis grauia, aut versus coelum leuia, velocius feruntur, quam sine Dei adminiculo, ad omnigenam fœditatem, humana caro. Paulus ad Romanos, Gentiles, Deum in mundi machina, legeque naturæ contemplantes, & tamen contemnentes, significat à Creatore, sibi suisque pollutionibus derelictos. {u}Tradidit eos Deus, cupiditatibus cordium ipsorum: atq; iterum, {x}Tradidit eos Deus fœdis affectibus: & tertio, {y}Tradidit eos Deus in sensum reprobum, vel in mentem omnis iudicij expertem. Sed & recensentur fructus, qui in agris istis sic incultis sunt enati; impuritas, & fœdatio suorum corporum, in libidine ardor, naturæ inuersa peruersio, & alia infinita. Nihil aliud Paulus significatum voluit, quam lepra quasi tetra, & contagione immedicabili eos teneri, quibus Deus timorem suum, & sacrosancti Spiritus influentiam salutarem sustulerit. Et quod omnibus non auferat, suæ plane est misericordiæ; quæ cum totum humanum genus, in Protoplasti crimine, nequitiæ vinculis involutum ita, deprehendisset, ut iuste possit singu-los condemnare, præ sua tamen benignitate, gratis, & gratuito, sevocavit aliquot, quibus spem cœlestis regni concessit, iisq; sacri Spiritus opem, afflatumq; impertiit: quo, in vitæ puritatem, & sanctitatem vergerent. Verum, hoc ipsius plane clementiæ tribuendum est; ut & severitati, iustitiæque suæ, quod cæteris hunc favorem non impendat. Cum tamen vultus lumen, benedictionemque subtraxerit, in quantas vitiorum sententias & colluvies, sua spōte reprobi illi prorumpunt? Originalis etenim maculæ radix, in amplam peccatorum segetem, nequit non pullulare: sicut in vepres, & urticas, necesse est terra excrescat, si colono dextra non accesserit. Unde, non inepte, perversorum fœditates, lapidibus, & saxis, in structuram fornicis, operisve arcuati comparantur, quorum pondus, columna subtus stante sustentatur, & suffulcitur. Si advenerit Samson aliquis, qui vindictam super Philistæos sumpturus, columnam, uno quasi ictu diruendo auferet, occasionem ille præstitit ruinæ domus: sed præ sua gravitate, saxa concident, ut quæ præter naturam suam, altiore loco repósita fuerunt. Non secus sese habet Omnipotentis manus; quæ cum gratiæ suæ solidum firmamentum subripuerit, sponte, mortalium mens in ruinam prolabetur. Attamen, ut gravitati lapidum acceptum ferendum est, quod deorsum provoluantur; sic hominis iniustitiæ, corruptæque cogitationi, adiudicandum est, quod in peccata præcipitetur. Ita, reus tenetur homo; innocens Deus; qui subtrahendo Spiritum, sensu aliquo, peccatum non vetare dicatur, neque tamen peccare facere.
units.tr: The Apostle often says to those to whom he writes: Before Christ had shone upon your hearts, you were Gentiles, without God in this world, defiled by filthiness, overwhelmed by wickedness. And however many there are on whom the Spirit does not shine, they are carried headlong into almost every kind of evil. Heavy things are not carried more swiftly to the earth, nor light things more swiftly towards heaven, than human flesh, without the help of God, is carried to every kind of filthiness. Paul, in Romans, signifies that the Gentiles, who contemplated God in the machinery of the world and in the law of nature, and yet despised him, were abandoned by the Creator to themselves and their pollutions. God gave them up to the lusts of their hearts (Rom. 1); and again, God gave them up to shameful affections; and a third time, God gave them up to a reprobate mind, or to a mind void of all judgement. But there are also listed the fruits which have sprung up in these fields so uncultivated: impurity and the defiling of their bodies, the burning of lust, the perversion of nature overturned, and countless others. Paul meant nothing else to be signified than that they are held by a leprosy, as it were foul, and an incurable contagion, whom God has removed from his fear and the saving influence of the most holy Spirit. And that he does not take this away from all is plainly a matter of his mercy; which, when it had found the whole human race entangled in the bonds of wickedness through the crime of the first parent, so that he could justly condemn each one, nevertheless, by his kindness, freely and by free gift, set apart some, to whom he granted the hope of the heavenly kingdom, and to whom he imparted the aid and inspiration of the holy Spirit, by which they might tend towards purity and holiness of life. Yet this is plainly to be ascribed to his clemency; so that it also belongs to his severity and justice that he does not bestow this favour on the rest. Yet when he has withdrawn the light of his countenance and his blessing, into how many judgements of vices and into what a filth do those reprobate break out of their own accord? For the root of original stain cannot fail to sprout into a broad crop of sins: just as thorns and nettles must necessarily grow from the earth, if the right hand of the farmer has not come to it. Whence, not unfittingly, the foulnesses of the perverse are compared to stones and rocks in the building of a vault or an arched structure, whose weight is sustained and propped up by a column standing beneath. If some Samson should come, about to take vengeance upon the Philistines, and, as it were with one blow, should remove the column to be destroyed, he has provided an occasion for the ruin of the house; but by their own weight the stones will fall, since they were placed, contrary to their nature, in a higher position. The hand of the Omnipotent is no different: when it has withdrawn the solid support of its grace, of its own accord the mind of mortals slips into ruin. Yet just as it must be credited to the weight of the stones that they roll downwards, so it must be adjudged to the injustice of man and his corrupt thought that he is hurled into sins. Thus man is held guilty; God is innocent; who, by withdrawing the Spirit, may be said not to forbid sin by some sense, and yet not to cause sin.

units.la: 7. Quarto, in ipsis actionibus, quæ ex humana parte vitiosæ sunt, Divinus plane elucescit digitus; sed ita, ut actionis, operisque motor sit, & impulsor Deus; non autē obliquitatis, aut curuitatis in agendo. Excitat enim Dominus Spiritus impiorū, ad nonnulla aggredienda, in quibus piorū probetur patienpatientia; aut suorum filiorum errata castigentur; aut supplicium pro atrocitate scelerum, & transgressionum, sumendum est:quae omnia, ex parte Creatoris sunt iustissima, & vel à ruga aliena, cum alio tamen affectu feratur homo impius;non pietatem, aut Diuinum respiciens obsequium, sed satisfactionem sui animi. {z}Quod mali peccant, ipsorum est, inquit Augustinus, quod vero peccando, hoc vel illud agant, ex virtute Dei est, tenebras prout visum est, diuidentis. Cū igitur vter-que, id est, Deus, & homo, iustus Deus, & iniustus homo, vnum, idemque volunt, & efficiunt; finis ob quem, & modus per quem vterque operatur, diuersam in vtrisq; opera-tionem,diuersum opus faciunt. Voluit {a}Deus Dauidis con-cubinas vitiari; quamuis non praeceperit. Et voluit Absalo-mus. At in Deo scopus erat praefixus, vt Dauidis adulterium castigaret; sicque, ipsum ad ampliorem, & arctiorem poenitentiam duceret. Absalomi autem meta erat alia; vt libidini nempe propriae satisfaceret, paternoque animo vulnus infligeret. {b}Suscitauit[?] Deus Jehu, vt Achabi progeniem funditus exterreret; quo tum transgressiones eius familiae vindicaret, tum suum compleret eloquium, ab Elia Prophe-ta pronunciatum. Vertiginosus autem spiritus ambitionis Jehu mentem occupauerat, vanae causa gloriae, in tribunal ascendere cupientis. Nostro saepe seculo contingit, vt sanguis sanguine puniatur. Qui occidit innocentes, ab alio, qui vt flagellum Dei immittitur (etiamsi homo prauus sit) interficitur. Operatur isthic Deus; operatur homo: iuste Deus, quia iuste puniens; pessime occisor, quia a-{c}uaritiae gratia, aut inuidiae interficiens. Forte {c}aliquis dicat, inquit Ambrosius, quomodo in parricidio, velin incestu, manus fuerit Dei, cum opus illud inimici sit. Cognoscamus igitur, quoniam & vbi Diabolus vulnerat, sagitta Domini vulnerare dicantur. Domini est poena, Diaboli malitia.
units.tr: 7. Fourthly, in the very actions which are sinful on the human side, the divine finger plainly shines forth; but in such a way that God is the mover and impeller of the action and the work, but not of the crookedness or perversity in acting. For the Lord stirs up the spirits of the impious to undertake certain things, in which the patience of the pious is tested; or the errors of his sons are chastised; or punishment must be exacted for the atrocity of crimes and transgressions: all of which, on the part of the Creator, are most just, and are far from any fault; yet the impious man is carried on with a different affection, looking not to piety or divine obedience, but to the satisfaction of his own mind. "That the wicked sin is their own," says Augustine, "but that by sinning they do this or that is from the power of God, who divides the darkness as it seems good to him." Therefore, since each, that is God and man, the just God and the unjust man, wills and effects one and the same thing, the end for which and the means by which each works make a different operation and a different work in each. God willed that the concubines of David should be violated, although he did not command it. And Absalom willed it too. But in God the mark was set, that he might chastise David's adultery and thus lead him to a fuller and stricter repentance. But Absalom's goal was another: namely, to satisfy his own lust and inflict a wound on his father's heart. God stirred up Jehu, so that he might utterly terrify the offspring of Ahab; by which he might at once avenge the transgressions of that family and fulfil his word, pronounced by the prophet Elijah. But the giddy spirit of ambition had occupied Jehu's mind, desiring to ascend the tribunal for the sake of empty glory. In our own age it often happens that blood is punished by blood. He who has killed the innocent is slain by another, who is sent as a scourge of God (even though he be a wicked man). God works there; man works there: God justly, because he punishes justly; the killer most wickedly, because he kills for the sake of greed or envy. "Perhaps someone will say," says Ambrose, "how the hand of God could be in parricide, or in incest, since that work belongs to the enemy. Let us therefore recognise both that and where the Devil wounds, it is said that the arrow of the Lord wounds. The punishment is the Lord's; the malice is the Devil's."

units.la: §. Augustinus super Exodum, de homine, per Deum, in manus impij occisoris tradito, sic loquitur: {d}Cum volens & ipse occidit, & Deus tradidit in manus eius, hoc interest, quod illic tantum Deus fecit, hic autem & Deus, & homo, propter voluntatem facientis, sed non facit Deus, ut homo. Deus enim non nisi iuste, homo autem poena dignus, non quia illum occidit, quem Deus nollet occidi, sed quia per iniquitatem, non enim ministerium Deo iubenti praebuit, sed sua maligna cupiditati seruiuit. Cum hic igitur suo indulges furori, actionem vitiauerit, operando longe diuersus est a Deo. Modus ideo, & finis, facta nostra bona, a malis, legitima ab illegitimis discriminant. Romani Magistratus capitis damnatos securi feriebant, saepissime; & recte, quia iustitiae exequendae gratia; & terrendi alios. At {e}Flaminius aliquando, in prandio sedens, damnatum captiuum accersi fecerat, & coram decollari. Pessime sane factum; quia non in beneficiū Reip, hoc praeceperat; sed ut Amasij desiderio, quod refert {f}Plutarchus, meretricis lasciuiae, quod {g}Hieronymus habet, morem gereret. Semper rationem, ordinemque facti attendamus; & purius fiet iudicium. Sed in una, & eadem re, voluntatum diuersitas diuersa producit. Decumbit fortassis in lecto moribundus pater, quem e viuis sublatum, Deus, filiusque cupiunt. Sed Omnipotens Deus, ut e valle miseriarum, ad aeterna, coelestiaque tabernacula amoueat: prodigus vero filius, ut extincto patre, hereditate perfrua-tur. Quid aequius in Deo? quid iniquius in filio? Ita sane operari, in iis Dominus cognoscitur, quae sunt mala, sed non quatenus sint mala, neque ut sint mala. Augustinus de gratia, & libero arbitrio, cum de praesenti materia disseruisset; digitumque Dei, in mouendo, & impellendo, versari docuisset, concludit tandem: {h}Satis quantum existimo, manifesta-tur: operari Deum in cordibus hominum; ad inclinandas eorum voluntates, quocunque voluerit, siue ad bona, pro sua misericordia, siue ad mala, pro meritis eorum, iudicio utique suo, aliquando aperto, aliquando occulto, semper autem iusto. Fixum enim esse debet, & immobile. bile in corde vestro, quia non est iniquitas apud Deum. Miror sane, quod Campianus ore patulo, in Augustinum non exclamarit; quod Deum dixerit, in cordibus sic operari, ut inclinet corda ad mala. Nihil aliud vult doctissimus Pater, quā quod nos volumus, inclinare Deum, homines; ad ea perficienda, quae ex humana parte mala sunt.
units.tr: §. Augustine, on Exodus, speaking of a man who is handed over by God into the hands of a wicked killer, says as follows: When a man, willing to kill, actually kills, and God delivers him into the killer's hands, the difference is this: God acts only in one way, but in the case of the killer both God and man act, because of the will of the doer; yet God does not act as the man does. For God acts only justly, whereas the man deserves punishment, not because he killed one whom God would not have wished killed, but because he acted wickedly: he did not offer his service to God's command, but served his own evil desire. So when he indulges his own rage here and spoils the action, in acting he is wholly unlike God. Therefore it is the manner and the end that distinguish our good deeds from evil ones and lawful acts from unlawful ones. The Roman magistrates very often struck the condemned with the axe, and rightly, because they did so to carry out justice and to terrify others. But Flaminius once, while sitting at dinner, had a condemned captive called in and beheaded before him. That was a very wicked deed, because he did not order it for the benefit of the commonwealth, but to gratify the desire of Amasius, as Plutarch reports, and the wanton lust of a prostitute, as Jerome has it. We should always attend to the reason and order of an action, and the judgment will be the clearer. But in one and the same deed, the diversity of wills produces diverse results. Perhaps a father lies dying in bed, whom God and his son both desire to take from the living: but the Almighty God does so to move him from the valley of miseries to the eternal and heavenly tabernacles; the prodigal son wishes it so that, with his father dead, he may enjoy the inheritance. What is more just in God? What is more unjust in the son? Thus the Lord is known to work in those things which are evil, yet not insofar as they are evil, nor so that they may be evil. Augustine, in his work on grace and free will, after he had discussed this present matter and taught that the finger of God works in moving and impelling, at last concludes: "It is sufficiently clear, I think, that God works in the hearts of men to incline their wills wherever He wills, whether to good, according to His mercy, or to evil, according to their merits, by His judgment indeed, sometimes open, sometimes hidden, but always just. For it must be fixed and immovable in your heart that there is no iniquity with God." I am indeed amazed that Campian did not cry out with open mouth against Augustine, because he said that God works in hearts in such a way as to incline them to evil. The most learned Father wants nothing other than what we ourselves want: that God incline men to bring to completion those things which, on the human side, are evil.

units.la: 9. Et quid aliud veritati coniunctius esse potest, quando certum est, neminem hominum aliquid posse operari, cui non adsit, & insit Deus? Ratum enim illud est, & inconcussae veritatis, de mortalibus omnibus, non de piis solis, quod {i}in Deo vivimus, movemur, & sumus. In ipso movemur, & ubique & perpetuo: ipse igitur nos mouet; & in omnibus. Sin, impulsi, nostra sponte transfuersim feramur, aut titubanter; id nostri vitii est. Actiones, & motus Dei sunt claudicationes, & exorbitationes nostrae. Non dissimilem supplet locum, in mente Dominus, atque in corpore anima, quae sensus, & roboris causa est, & è loco profectionis. Si habilia, idoneaque membra, praestantior nostri pars reperit; en, ordine fiunt omnia. Sin arescat brachium, sicut {k}Ieroboamo aliquando, ut fortiter; & robuste non possit manus rapere, aut commode contrectare; aut genua sint debilia, infirmaque crura, ut corporis molem sufferre nequeant, sicque haesitanter, & titubanter eatur, in membra haec inualida, non in animam culpa reiiciatur. Talis est Omnipotentis ἐνέργεια in nobis; quae, si rectam animi dispositionem inuenerit, pia facit esse opera, & talia; quae laude digna sunt. Quod si mala mente, motum eius, & impulsionem capiamus, & in transuersa oblique, perperamque exiliamus, id nostrae culpae est. Non inepte, ad faciliorem tanti scrupuli expeditionem, his similibus res omnis illustrari queat. In eorum rerum venalium, suum famulum, dominus necessaria mercatum mittit. Sed seruuli ea est improbitas, & petulantia, ut in via pugnis quenquam obuium caedat, aut in foro furtum faciat. Si de facto fiat quæstio, respondebit dominus se in causa fuisse, quamobrem è priuata familia puer discesserit, in plateam ierit, in forum venerit; quod autem inter eundum, iniuria quenquam lacessierit, aut quid clam subripuerit, id alterius esse; puerilis scilicet proteruiæ: per ipsum non stare, quin pœnas luat. Rei igitur causa est, & author, sed non malæ rei, inter agendum perpetratæ. Theologi recentiores in istis exprimendis Similitudine alia mire commoda, vti consueuerunt. Cum ad iter, peregre quisquā profecturus, se accinxerit, equum conscendit. Qui voluit stare sonipes, & fræna, non ferox spumantia mandere, ex virga, aut calcare equitantis, ad motum, imo cursum incitatur. Quis negauerit, impulsorem esse solum equitem? Sed inter movendum, parum equus promouet, quia pede claudicante impeditur. Deformis hic est motus, & inutilis cursus, qui sessorem fortassis, vt excandescat, provocat. Quis sessori, claudicationem istam crimini dabit? Ita plane Deus noster, vt in multa incitemur, causa est, neque certe moueremur, nisi ipse incitasset. Sed quum claudi in inceflu, in operando vitiosi appareamus, hoc nostrum est, & nō Dei. Sua igitur potentia, & æterna præsentia, integra Domino permaneat, qua impiis etiam adest, sed non vt sint impii. Nihilo magis, ille labem, aut maculā contrahit, ex præposteris suarum creaturarum actionib. quam ex putrido cadauere, aut simeto. Solis radii vitium sordesque colligunt. Innocuus, & integer, & omni modo ἀναμάρτητος permanet Omnipotens, fœces hominis, vt ab homine ortas relinquens. Ex sese[?] vnico est perditio Israelis, sed salus eius à Deo. Et hactenus, de quarto doctrinæ nostræ fundamento.
units.tr: 9. And what can be more closely bound to the truth than this, since it is certain that no man can do anything without God being present to him and within him? For that saying is firm and of unshaken truth, concerning all mortals and not only the pious: "In God we live, move, and have our being." In Him we move, both everywhere and continually; He therefore moves us, and in all things. But if, when impelled, we are carried sideways of our own accord, or stumblingly, that is the fault of our vice. The actions and motions of God are our limpings and deviations. The soul, which is the cause of sense and strength and the starting-point of motion, fills a similar place in the body as the Lord does in the mind. If our members are fit and suitable, the better part of us finds them; behold, all things are done in order. But if an arm withers, as once happened to Jeroboam, so that the hand cannot seize strongly and firmly, or touch conveniently; or if the knees are weak and the legs feeble, so that they cannot bear the weight of the body, and one walks hesitantly and stumblingly, the fault is not to be laid on the soul but on these feeble members. Such is the energy of the Almighty in us: which, if it finds a right disposition of mind, makes works pious and such as are worthy of praise. But if we take its motion and impulse with an evil mind and leap crookedly and perversely to one side, that is the fault of our own guilt. This whole matter can be illustrated not unsuitably by similar things, for the easier removal of so great a scruple. A master sends his servant to buy the necessary goods at the market. But the servant's disposition is so wicked and petulant that on the way he strikes someone he meets with his fists, or steals something in the marketplace. If the matter is inquired into, the master will answer that he was the cause of the boy's leaving the private household, going into the street and coming to the market; but that the wrong he did to someone on the way, or what he secretly snatched, belongs to another: namely, to the boy's own puerile wantonness; it is not through the master that the boy does not pay the penalty. So the master is the cause and author of the thing, but not of the evil thing committed in the course of the action. More recent theologians, in setting forth these matters, have been accustomed to use another, remarkably apt comparison. When someone who is about to set out on a journey has girded himself, he mounts a horse. The horse, which would prefer to stand still, and does not champ the bit fiercely and foaming, is spurred on by the whip or the heel of the rider, to motion, indeed to a gallop. Who would deny that the rider alone is the impeller? But in moving, the horse makes little progress, because it is hindered by a limping foot. This motion is misshapen and this course useless, and perhaps it provokes the rider to anger. Who will impute that limping to the rider? So plainly our God is the cause that we are stirred into much, and certainly we would not move unless He had stirred us. But since we appear lame in walking, faulty in acting, this is ours and not God's. His power, then, and His eternal presence remain whole for the Lord, by which He is present even to the impious, but not so that they may be impious. No more does He contract a stain or blemish from the perverse actions of His creatures than from a rotting corpse or a dung-heap. The rays of the sun gather filth and foulness, yet remain innocent, whole, and in every way ἀναμάρτητος [sinless], the Almighty leaving the dregs to man, as arising from man. "Your destruction is from yourself alone, O Israel, but your help is from God." And so far concerning the fourth foundation of our teaching.

units.la: 10. Sed & quintum adhuc est, non indignum quod addatur, Israelitis[?] moderandis, & dispensandis hominum, bo-num sane ob finem, (quantum ad ipsum spectat) ea submittit Deus, & offert, quæ per ipsorum abusum & applicatione prauam, malis occasiones sunt peccatorum suorum. Sed, quod ad mala, vel improbus, vel regeneratus, haec oblata peruertat: id ipsorum est, Formosam foeminam, coram homine libidinoso hac, illac transfire, vt infirmos aegrosque visitet: aut ad Deum in Ecclesia colendum vadere, instigat Dominus. Hinc, adulter, opportunitatem libidine exardescendi nanciscitur. {m}Vt vidi, vt perii. Parum sane dubitamus quin ex speciali Dei voluntate fuerit, vt Bethsabe, se obo-culos {n}Dauidis ablueret: quod vero in adulterium otiosus Rex proruperit, Dauidis fuerat, qui suis moderari, & imperare affectibus tunc temporis non didicisset. Num vestis illa {o}Babylonica & argenti massa, Achano in tentationem, & offendiculum fuisset, nisi suo consilio Dominus decreuisset & determinasset, talia irritamenta ipsius conspectui proponenda? Obtulit igitur occasionem caelestis Pater; sed quam homo pius euitasset, Achanus est amplexus. Sicut igitur, in Offensis distinguere consueuimus, esse Scandalum datum, & Scandalum acceptum: acceptum saepe Scandalum, cum non datur, sic, porrigitur a Deo aliquid; quod in se non est malum, & tamen a persona accipiente, in peccatum transmutatur. Medicamentum, quod a Medico ad choleram expurgadam subministratur, cum in stomachum cholera oppressum, & repletum inciderit, & ipsum etiam in choleram conuertitur. Num ex Medici errore, hoc factum est, an potius a stomacho, aut ventriculo, humore putrido exundante, proficisciter[?]? Verum tamen, cum infirmi, omniumque fragilissimi naturae simus; & nisi afflatus ille caelestis, & Paracletus adstiterit, leuiculo omni vento, in discrimen inextri-cabile ruituri, orandus est Deus, & assidue implorandus, vt {p}in tentationem nos non inducat. Cuilibet enim ea gratiae mensura non est concessa, quae Abrahamo, qua vique ad vnici sui filii immolationem, immobilis stare poterat. Precandum est, vt {q}auertat Deus oculos nostros, ne videant vanitatem, vt cohii cohibeat linguam, sicut ostio, aut fræno. Aut si fidei, & patientiæ explorandæ causa, nos velit in probationem, tentationemque ducere, vt à {r}malo tamen liberare dignetur, ne oneri succumbamus, & auxilio salutari destituti, in perniciem incurramus. Et certe isthæc opportunitatum ad peccandū suppeditatio, per hominum improbitatem, grandis deuandi est occasio.
units.tr: 10. But there is still a fifth point, not unworthy to be added, concerning the ordering and disposing of men: God, indeed for a good end (as far as it concerns Himself), submits and offers those things which, through their abuse and wrong application, become occasions of sin for the evil. But that the wicked, or even the regenerate, pervert what is offered them for evil is their own doing. That a beautiful woman passes this way and that before a lustful man, so that she may visit the sick and infirm, or go to worship God in the Church, the Lord inspires; from this the adulterer finds an opportunity to burn with lust. "As soon as I saw her, I perished." We hardly doubt that it was by the special will of God that Bathsheba washed herself in the sight of David; but that the idle king broke out into adultery was David's fault, who had not then learned to moderate and govern his own passions. Would that Babylonian garment and the mass of silver have been a temptation and a stumbling-block to Achan, had not the Lord by His own counsel decreed and determined that such enticements be set before His sight? Thus the heavenly Father offered the occasion; but what a pious man would have avoided, Achan embraced. Therefore, just as in the matter of offences we are accustomed to distinguish between a scandal given and a scandal taken, and often a scandal is taken where none is given, so something is extended by God which in itself is not evil, and yet in the receiving person is turned into sin. A medicine which is administered by a physician to purge choler, when it falls upon a stomach oppressed and filled with choler, is itself also turned into choler. Did this happen through the physician's error, or rather because the stomach or belly overflows with putrid humour? Nevertheless, since we are weak and the most frail of all creatures, and unless that heavenly breath and the Paraclete stand by us, we would fall into an inextricable danger at the slightest breeze, God must be prayed to and continually implored that He not lead us into temptation. For the measure of grace that was granted to Abraham, by which he could stand immovable even to the sacrifice of his only son, is not granted to everyone. We must pray that God "turn away our eyes, lest they see vanity," and that He restrain the tongue as with a door or a bridle. Or if He wills to lead us into proof and temptation for the sake of trying our faith and patience, that He deign nonetheless to deliver us from evil, so that we do not sink under the burden and, deprived of saving help, run into destruction. And certainly this supplying of opportunities for sinning, through the wickedness of men, is a great occasion for stumbling.

units.la: II. Nonnunquam contingit, vt, cum acerbæ inimicitiæ inter duos emerserint, sceleratos forsitan, & infames vtrosque, quorum alterum, pro flagello, virgaque, alteri esse Deus constituit, vt vel venatum, aut aucupatum, aut commoda quæsitum, hominem morti destinatum mundi Rectorem emittat, & ita, vt hosti armato, necesse est occurrat, qui licet (legum metu coactus) manus libens noluerit conserere, nedum occidere, furoris tamen, stomachique violentia impulsus, & aggreditur, & ferro perimit. Occisum occisor non quæsiisset, sed datum obtruncauit. Malitiosa profecto mente, ideoque peccans: Cum alium habuerit Deus operandi scopum, nempe, vt scelestos è medio tolleret, & pœnas requirendo, nomen suum glorificaret. Et, vt, quod verum est, hac in re fatear, tales occasiones sic ingerendo, nonnunquam Dominus, ea, quæ ex se sunt benedictiones, in seuerius iudicium, & profundiorem maledictionem, & condemnationem reproborum, succedere permittit. Ministerium Verbi, est ipsum organum, & instrumentum salutis animarum: ita vt, quibus id Æternus dispensator impertire cognoscatur, benedictionem impendere merito videatur. Sed cum populo immorigero virisque peruicacibus prædicatum fuerit, quorum oculi obcæcantur, ne videant, & incrassantur corda, ne intelligant, in ruinam grandiorem, futura est hæc Verbi auditio, quia sermo, qui profertur ex præconis ore, in iudicio testimonium aduersum, damnāsque est perhibiturus. Facilius e-nim Tyro, & Sidoni, quam vrbibus Chorazin, & Bethsaida. Admonitiones Ministrorum, durioris rebellionis auditores conuincunt & coarguunt. Et quod adhuc est amplius, delusiones impostorum, & Antichristi, sic & lapsus sanctorum, ob oculos repraesentari reprobis, & Idola colentibus, facit Dominus, vt qui veneno delectantur, venenum exugant, cum interea quae apis esset, ex eo potius flore mel conficeret. Sic in Antichristi sectatoribus factum est, vt Miracula falsa conspiciendo, in reprobum magis sensum tradantur, puniente illic Deo duritiam cordis, non peccante. Ieroboamus aliquando, cui Deus sui vultus lumen, gratiamq; subduxisset, tanquam Idolis seruiens, in aeternam ruinam proculdubio est destinatus. Aduertite tamen, quas ansas huic praebuit Creator omnium, vt in superstitioso vitulorum cultu pergeret. ‡ Accessit Propheta, qui aris Ieroboami, & sacrificantibus, dira minabatur; quem cum Rex vellet comprehendere, exarescente immediate dextra palam plectitur. Cum nec voce, nec miraculo, nec verbo Prophetico, nec malo suo, edoceri adhuc Princeps voluisset, quin in malitia perseueraret, excitauit occasionem commodiorem, iustus iudex, qua impulsus, ad suam perniciem, Rex infidelis perrexerat.
units.tr: II. It sometimes happens that, when bitter enmity has arisen between two men, both perhaps wicked and infamous, one of whom God has appointed as a scourge and rod for the other, the Ruler of the world sends the man destined for death out on a hunt, or on a fowling expedition, or in search of some advantage, and so he meets his enemy armed, as he must. The other, though constrained by fear of the laws, is unwilling to lift his hand to fight, much less to kill; yet impelled by the violence of rage and anger, he attacks and slays him with the sword. The slayer did not seek to kill the one who was killed, but struck him down when he was given into his hands. He acted with a malicious mind, and therefore sinned, although God had another aim in view: namely, to remove the wicked from the midst and, by requiting them with punishment, to glorify his own name. And, to confess what is true in this matter, by thus bringing about such occasions, the Lord sometimes permits things which are in themselves blessings to turn into a more severe judgment and a deeper curse and the condemnation of the reprobate. The ministry of the Word is itself the organ and instrument of the salvation of souls, so that it rightly seems to bestow a blessing upon those to whom the Eternal Dispenser is known to impart it. But when it is preached to an unruly people and to stubborn men, whose eyes are blinded so that they do not see, and whose hearts are hardened so that they do not understand, this hearing of the Word will turn to a greater ruin, for the word that is spoken from the mouth of the herald will bear witness against them in judgment and will condemn them. For it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon than for the cities of Chorazin and Bethsaida. The admonitions of ministers convict and reprove the hearers of a harder rebellion. And, what is more, the Lord causes the delusions of impostors and of Antichrist, and likewise the falls of the saints, to be set before the eyes of the reprobate and of those who worship idols, so that those who delight in poison suck out the poison, whereas the bee would rather make honey from that same flower. Thus it has come about among the followers of Antichrist that, by looking upon false miracles, they are given over to a more reprobate mind, God punishing the hardness of their heart there, though he does not sin. Jeroboam, from whom God had at some point withdrawn the light of his countenance and his grace, serving idols as he did, was undoubtedly destined to eternal ruin. Notice, however, what occasions the Creator of all things offered him, so that he should persist in the superstitious worship of the calves. ‡ A prophet came who threatened dire things against the altar of Jeroboam and against those who sacrificed; when the king wished to seize him, his hand immediately withered and he was openly struck. Since the prince had not been willing to be taught, neither by voice, nor by miracle, nor by the prophetic word, nor by his own harm, to refrain from persevering in wickedness, the just judge stirred up a more convenient occasion, by which the unfaithful king, driven on to his own destruction, proceeded.

units.la: {ꝏ} Ambitiosus, iuxta habitauerat Propheta, qui prioris Prophetae gloriae inuidens (ne fama & existimatione, apud populum praeiret) ad eundem accessit, & mendacium excogitans, in nomine Domini, in domum suam illum reduxit, cibumq; comedere coegit; qua ob causam iratus & excandescens Deus, leonē misērat, qui non obsequentem occideret.
units.tr: {ꝏ} An ambitious prophet had lived near the former prophet; envying the glory of that prophet, so that he should not surpass him in fame and esteem among the people, he went to him, devised a lie in the name of the Lord, led him back to his house and compelled him to eat food. For this cause God, angry and inflamed, sent a lion, which slew the one who did not obey.

units.la: {x} Iosephus hanc historiā recitans, occasionē à Domino suppeditatam arbitratur, ex qua peruersus Rex in nequitia sua perstaret, & permaneret. Cum enim, oculis suis occisum nūcium videret, cogitauit extemplo ipsum, impostorē esse, & non ex oraculo Diuino, sed è suo cerebro, exitium, in altari adolentibus interminatum fuisse. Quo pacto tamque, vere possit submonere alios, qui cauere sibi nequiret? Et cū istud multoties senior Propheta, qui decepit, ingeminaret, audaciam sumpsit Princeps, ut in vomitu suo versari perpe-tuo, non trepidaret. Ita Deus operatur, proponendo homi-nibus ea aliquando, quæ quamuis ex Dei parte sint iustissi-ma, malæ tamen menti sunt offendiculo, & titubationi. Professorum Euangelii lapsus, & notabilis error, aliquibus nostro tempore, in Papismo induratis, ita dati Scandali vicem supplet, ut refractarios magis illos, ac ab Euangelio auersos faciat.
units.tr: {x} Josephus, relating this history, thinks that the occasion was supplied by the Lord, from which the perverse king might persist and remain in his wickedness. For when he saw with his own eyes the messenger slain, he immediately thought that the prophet was an impostor, and that the threatened destruction at the altar had not come from a divine oracle but from his own brain. In what way, then, could he truly warn others, who could not beware for themselves? And since the deceiving old prophet repeated this many times, the prince took boldness, so that he did not tremble to wallow in his vomit perpetually. So God works, setting before men at times those things which, although they are most just on God's part, are yet a stumbling block and a cause of stumbling to a wicked mind. The lapse and notable error of the professors of the Gospel, in our time, serves in the same way as an occasion of offence to some who have been hardened in Popery, so that it makes them the more obstinate and turned away from the Gospel.

units.la: 12. Ex istis modo quasi iactis fundamentis, operantem Dei manum considerare licet, quo pacto Agens in omnibus reperiatur, sed non Author peccati. Reuocetur in mentem, quod primo patefactum est; non creatione Diuina, sed vitio hominis, & Satanæ, accessisse peccatu. Secundo quod mali nihil contingit, nisi permittente Domino. Tertio, quod subducit ipse aliquibus gratiam, & sic in peccata ruitur. Quarto, quod in omnibus quibuscunque demum actionibus est motus diuinus; sed non in claudicatione, exorbitatione, & obliquitate. Quinto, offerri ea per Dominum, quæ quanquam in se non sint flagitiosa, impiorum tamen cogitata, per innatam ipsorum prauitatem, ad ἀνομίαν[?] incitant. Ex istis non est difficile, in Scripturis, omnibus, quæ ex aduerso videntur stare, incolumē, integramq; iustitiam & sanctitatem Numinis conseruare. Ut igitur ei, primo occurratur loco, quod huius Quæstionis ventilandæ causam subministrauit, Regesilli, & Principes, qui Meretrici[?] Apo-{y}calyptice, imperia subdiderunt, fornicationem suam supre-mæ Maiestati referre non debent. Quamuis etenim à Deo proficiscatur aliquid; à sese tamen malum. Deus igitur iis posuit in corda, ut Bestiæ se consociarent. Subducendo illius spiritum, id ipsis in mentem venit: Cuius cum amotionis, Deus ipse causa sit; humano loquendo more, dicitur ipsis in animum suggessisse. Iterum, Antichristum multa facere perpessus est, quæ ad eius obsequium, fluctuantes & incre-dulos pellicere possint, & accersere ad scortationem. Tertio ipsis in mentem indidit, vt ea agerent, quæ quamquam peri-niquitatem agentiū transuersa fuerint, & immutata in ma-litiam, alium tamen ob finem, à Domino facta sunt: vt Pro-phetias scilicet expleret suas: vt puniret fortassis inobedi-entiam hominum: vt iustiorem ipsorum condemnationem fa-ceret. Cum illud citatur, Deum esse, qui mala condit in ci-uitate, respondent Scholastici; sed ante illos Tertullianus. Marcionitis etenim dicentibus, Deum esse authorem mali, quia scribitur: Ego sum, qui condo mala, respondet Tertul-lianus, esse mala quæ sunt delicta, & mala quæ sunt supplicia: mala quæ sunt culpæ; & mala quæ sunt pœnæ: illorum auto-rem esse Diabolum; horū, Deum creatorem. Trita ista sunt, & cuique obuia, neciis immorabimur.
units.tr: 12. From these foundations, so to speak, just laid, it is possible to consider the hand of God at work, and how he is found to be the Agent in all things, and yet not the Author of sin. Let it be recalled what has first been made plain: that sin came in not by divine creation but by the fault of man and of Satan. Second, that nothing evil happens except with the Lord permitting it. Third, that he himself withdraws grace from some, and so they fall into sin. Fourth, that in all actions whatsoever there is divine motion, but not in the limping, the deviation and the crookedness. Fifth, that things are offered by the Lord which, although in themselves they are not shameful, nevertheless stir up the thoughts of the impious to lawlessness [ἀνομία] through their innate wickedness. From these points it is not difficult, in all the Scriptures, to preserve the integrity and holiness of the Deity intact, even where things seem to stand against it. So, to meet first the point which furnished the occasion for discussing this question: the kings and princes who gave their power to the Apocalyptic Harlot ought not to refer their fornication to the supreme Majesty. For although something proceeds from God, evil nevertheless comes from themselves. God, therefore, put it into their hearts to join themselves with the Beast. By withdrawing his Spirit, this thought came into their minds; and since God himself is the cause of that withdrawal, it is said, in human manner of speaking, to have been suggested to their minds. Again, Antichrist has suffered many things which can entice the wavering and unbelieving to his obedience and draw them on to harlotry. Third, he put into their minds to do those things which, although they were perverse in the eyes of those who did them, and turned into malice, were nevertheless done by the Lord for another end: namely, to fulfil his own prophecies, perhaps to punish the disobedience of men, and to make their condemnation more just. When it is cited that it is God who creates evil in a city, the Schoolmen reply; but before them Tertullian did. For when the Marcionites said that God is the author of evil, because it is written: "I am he who creates evil," Tertullian replies that there are evils which are faults and evils which are punishments; the authors of the former is the Devil, of the latter God the Creator. These things are worn and common, and to everyone at hand; we shall not linger on them.

units.la: 13. De Pharaone legimus apud Mosen, quod indurasset cor eius Dominus: quod videtur significare originem malorum, à Dei duriore animo profectam esse. Respondet Origenes, Indurat Deus non agendo, sed patiendo, & non perden-do, ac si dominus lenis de seruo malo diceret: Ego eum perdidi, & cor-rupi: non docendo malum, sed non puniendo pro malo. Permissio-nem Diuinam & tolerantiam, accendisse ipsi stomachum censet. Vere quidè: at est aliquid amplius, quod habet Au-gustinus; Non obdurat Deus, impertiendo malitiam, sed non imper-tiendo misericordiam. Quod idem est, acsi diceret, contigisse obdurationem, quia Deus subduxit gratiam. Verissime, si quid aliud; sed & tertium superest. Cum etenim, mollities cordis, & obsequendi aptitudo, per subtractionem Spiritus sublata fuisset: misit Mosen Deus quouis die, qui verbū pro-ferendo, & signa ostendendo, pectus eius de integro percel-leret. Cum promoueret tamen nihil, ad obdurationem cor-dis posteriora hæc fecerunt, & transgressionem insigniore. Sed hoc ex ipsius fuerat corrupta prius natura, nō ex Verbo aut Miraculis. Non possunt ista comparari melius, quam fa-bri malleo; qui si candens ferrum, & igne emollitum percus-serit, in varias (licet ferrū sit) figuras efformat: sin, in metal-lum frigidum, aut in cutem recidat, nihil aliud, quam duri-tiem crassiorem impertit. Incrassato ex se, callosoque cordi Pharaonis, accesserunt sermones Mosis; è quibus in maiorē & rigidiorem obdurationem creuit. De Dauide vnum est, quod multis iniecit scrupulum; sine causa profecto, {e}Incita-uit Deus, inquiunt, Dauidē, vt numeraret populum. Et pu-niuit tandē. Quod punierit tam seuere, manifestum est pec-catū fuisse. Et cum moueret Deus, vt faceret, quid ni author peccati fuerat? {f}Annotarunt Geneuenses, incitasse Deum, Dauidem, id est, Satanæ permisisse, vt incitaret. Et interpre-tatione suam è libro Chronicorum stabiliunt: vbi expressis dixit verbis Spiritus Sanctus, stetisse Satanā aduersus Israe-lem, & prouocasse Dauidem, vt Israelem numeraret. At pe-nitius aliquando adhuc, doctissimeq; & sanctissime, Treme-lius, & Iunius, qui in textu è Samuele, non Dominū, sed Ad-uersarium, id est, Satanam, Dauidem fuscitasse exponunt, & sic legunt, perrexit autem ira Iehoua, accendi in Israelitas; quum in-citasset aduersarius Dauidem in eos, dicendo age, numera Israelem, & Iehudam. Vbi vocem, aduersarius, minusculis literis è suo adiii-ciunt supplemento: sed adhibita ratione, ex phrasi Sacris li-teris familiari; vbi Nomina Coniugata, Verbis suis; vt è contra Verba Nominibus inclusa latent. Ita in Verbo incitandi, la-tet Incitator, id est, ad malum, Dæmon: in Aduersando, Ad-uersarius. Non est igitur, vt de illo solliciti simus testimonio, cum à Dæmone, ad peccatum commotum Dauidem, asse-ratur.
units.tr: 13. We read in Moses about Pharaoh that the Lord hardened his heart; which seems to signify that the origin of evils proceeded from a harder mind of God. Origen replies: "God hardens not by acting but by suffering, and not by destroying, as if a gentle master were to say of a wicked servant: I have destroyed him and corrupted him; not by teaching evil, but by not punishing for evil." He thinks that the divine permission and tolerance kindled his anger. Truly so; but Augustine has something more: "God does not harden by imparting malice, but by not imparting mercy." This is the same as if he said that the hardening came about because God withdrew grace. Most truly, if anything; but there is also a third thing. For when the softness of the heart and the aptness for obeying had been taken away by the withdrawal of the Spirit, God sent Moses every day, who, by uttering the word and showing signs, would strike his breast anew. But since he accomplished nothing, these later things produced hardening of the heart and a more serious transgression. But this came from his nature, already corrupted beforehand, not from the Word or the miracles. These things cannot be better compared than to the smith's hammer: if it strikes glowing iron, softened by fire, it shapes it into various forms (though the iron is still iron); but if it falls upon cold metal or upon hide, it imparts nothing but a coarser hardness. To Pharaoh's heart, thickened and callous of its own accord, the words of Moses came; and from these his obduracy grew into a greater and more rigid hardness. There is one thing about David which has put a stumbling block in the way of many: "Without cause, surely, God incited David," they say, "to number the people." And at last he punished him. That he punished him so severely shows clearly that it was a sin. And since God moved him to do it, why would he not be the author of sin? The Geneva annotators noted that God incited David, that is, permitted Satan to incite him. And they confirm their interpretation from the book of Chronicles, where the Holy Spirit expressly said that Satan stood against Israel and provoked David to number Israel. But more deeply still, and most learnedly and most holily, Tremellius and Junius, who in the text from Samuel explain that it was not the Lord but the Adversary, that is, Satan, who stirred up David, and so read: "And the anger of the Lord burned against Israel again; when the Adversary had incited David against them, saying: Go, number Israel and Judah." Where they add the word "adversary" in lower-case letters as a supplement of their own; but, by a method drawn from the phrase familiar in Sacred Scripture, where the names are joined to their verbs, just as the verbs are hidden within the names. Thus in the verb "to incite" the Inciter lies hidden, that is, the demon who urges to evil; in "to oppose," the Adversary. There is therefore no need for us to be troubled by that testimony, since it is asserted that David was moved to sin by a demon.

units.la: 14. Exhis quæ dicta sunt, difficile non est; & aliis, quot-quot fuerint, occurrere, secundū fidei analogiam. De {h}Se-hone Regehesbon per Deum obdurato, vt Israelitis transi-tum non daret: & de reliquis {i}populis, qui etiam in Canaane;à Domino indurati perhibentur, respondere pauciss licet; vt de Pharaone: Subduxit Deus gratiam, & occasionees datas, in perniciē eorum conuerti passus est. Iussit Deus {k}Shimei, vt Dauidi conuicia, & cōtumelias intentaret: Hoc est, constituit Deus linguam Shimei; tanquam flagellū Dauidi; vt ipsum peccantem corrigeret, & castigaret. In quo, cum Dominus poenam, & iustitiæ executione, humiliationem scilicet Regis spectaret; sed homo malitiosus, vt conuiciando, irę; & libidini suæ perplaceret; male fecit Shimei, iustissime Deus. / {l}Roboamo Deus author fuit, vt stulte loquendo ad populum, decem Tribus vno die perderet. Non quod Roboamo immiserit imprudentiam, sed prudentiam detraxerit. Hinc, Seniorum contemptum est consilium. Et Iuniores praesto esse voluit Deus, qui pessima suaderent; quibus eneruato prius ingenio, & mente, necesse fuit, vt Roboamus auscultaret. Adeoque amplius, Prophetici sermonis sui per Abiam, complementum; & poenam in familiam Salomonis (propter Idololatriam) & in multas Tribus, quæ vt probabile est, simul cum Rege suo Salomone, fornicatæ fuissent; respexit: Roboamus puerili suo satisfactum voluit animo: Ieroboamus ambitioso Regni desiderio æstuauit: scopus Dei, erat sola iustitia; & veritas. {m}Dominus mendacem posuit spiritum, in ore Pseudo prophetarum, qui Achabo astiterunt: hoc est, permisit Satanæ, vt Zedechias, & socii apud Regem, mendaciter effutirent sua. Vbi, cum Satanas Achabi interitum captaret, dum Deo cuperet inobsequentem reddere; supplicium, super hominem incredulum, & homicidam, meta fuerat vnica, ad quam lehoua collimauit: De spiritu vertiginis, & soporis immitti dicto, & de eo etiam; {n}Quare errare nos fecisti Domine de viis tuis, indurasti cor nostrum, ne timeremus te; respondendum est, vt supra, per subtractionem gratiæ, & misericordiæ non donationem; partim ista fieri, & partim, quod opportunitates. tes tentationum Deus præbeat, quib. ipsi succumbunt. Non est, quod infinitus sim, in Scripturæ authoritatibus discutiendis, cum eadem vniuersi Sacri Codicis sit ratio, & supremum Numen illud, quod vnicum, gloria, & honore, & immortalitate dignum est, à labe alienum, à crimine immune, perpetuo stat.
units.tr: 14. Of these things that have been said, it is not difficult, and it is possible to meet all others, however many there are, according to the analogy of faith. Concerning Sihon, king of Heshbon, hardened by God so that he would not give the Israelites passage, and concerning the other peoples who are also said to have been hardened by the Lord, even in Canaan, a few things may be answered, as with Pharaoh: God withdrew his grace and allowed the occasions given to be turned to their destruction. God commanded Shimei to heap insults and abuse upon David; that is, God set Shimei's tongue as a scourge for David, so that he might correct and chastise him in his sin. In this, since the Lord looked to punishment and the execution of justice, namely the humbling of the king, but the wicked man, in order to satisfy his anger and his lust by reviling, acted badly, Shimei acted badly, while God acted most justly. / God was the author of Rehoboam's speaking foolishly to the people, by which he lost the ten tribes in a single day. Not that God infused imprudence into Rehoboam, but that he withdrew prudence from him. Hence he scorned the counsel of the elders. And God willed that the young men be at hand, who would advise the worst; and once his mind and spirit had been weakened, it was necessary that Rehoboam listen to them. And moreover, God looked to the fulfilment of his prophetic word spoken through Abijah, and to the punishment upon the house of Solomon (on account of idolatry) and upon the many tribes which, as is probable, had committed fornication together with their king Solomon. Rehoboam wished to satisfy his childish spirit; Jeroboam burned with the ambitious desire of the kingdom; the aim of God was simply justice and truth. The Lord put a lying spirit in the mouth of the false prophets who stood by Ahab; that is, he permitted Satan that Zedekiah and his companions at the king's court should utter their own lies falsely. Here, while Satan sought Ahab's destruction, desiring to make him disobedient to God, the punishment of the unbelieving and murderous man was the only goal toward which Jehovah aimed. Concerning the spirit of stupor and deep sleep being sent, and concerning that also: Why, O Lord, have you made us wander from your ways, and hardened our heart, so that we did not fear you? it must be answered, as above, that it happens through the withdrawal of grace and mercy, not through its bestowal; partly these things happen, and partly God furnishes the opportunities of temptation to which they yield. There is no need for me to be lengthy in examining the authorities of Scripture, since the reasoning of the whole sacred Codex is the same, and that supreme Deity, which alone is worthy of glory, honour and immortality, stands forever free from stain and immune from crime.

units.la: 15. Quoniam tamen, nihil quicquam ad negotium incumbens, illustrius esse potest, quam Christi Saluatoris nostri cædes; & crucifixio, vno quasi verbo, de ea dicendum est. Cum enim insignis illa fuerat præuaricatio in populo; quod innocuum Dei Agnum ad mortem duxerint, sicque, filii Omnipotentis, sanguine manus suas commacularint; & cum Iudas, si quis vnquam alius, in ipso prodendo, peccatum aduersus Spiritum Sanctum perpetrarit, cui nulla vnquam futura erat remissio, à Petro{o} tamen, facta esse dicitur hæc crucifixio, definito consilio, & præstituto Dei. Quare igitur, id, crimini hominibus duxit Deus, quod futurum ipse nouerat; permiserat, statuerat; & in quo, si alicubi, suus digitus eluxerat? Non immerito. Alium etenim ob finem, occisum voluit Pater filium; ob alium Diabolus; ob tertium, Iudas; & quartum, populus. Isti siquidem vt parerent Sacerdotibus, & Principibus, ille, vt pecuniam, suæ proditionis precium lucraretur: Dæmon, vt mundi Saluatorem è medio tolleret; sed Creator Cœlestis, vt ex morte Vnigeniti, redemptio electorum, & ab æterna seruitute liberatio præstaretur. Audite Origenem. {p}Deus tradidit Christum, propter misericordiam circa genus humanum, quod vnico filio non pepercit; sed pro omnibus nobis tradidit eum. Cæteri autem tradiderunt eum iniquo proposito, vnusquisque secundum malitiam suam; Iudas propter auaritiam, Sacerdotes propter inuidiam, Diabolus propter timorem, ne auelleret de manu eius genus humanum per doctrinam ipsius. Ita, modum, & finem distinguit Origenes, operationum Diuinæ, & humanæ, in nece Christi; sed diserte nostro instituto, applicando, & colligen-do, non accommodat, vt inde excusat Deum; & aecuset ho-minem; id quod pie, & eleganter, facit Augustinus, trib. lo-cis diuersis, qui sensu conueniunt.
units.tr: 15. Since, however, nothing bearing on our business can be more illustrious than the slaying and crucifixion of Christ our Saviour, something must be said about it, in a word, as it were. For although that notable transgression was committed among the people, in that they led the innocent Lamb of God to death, and so with the blood of the Son of the Almighty defiled their hands; and although Judas, if anyone ever did, committed in the very betrayal a sin against the Holy Spirit, for which there was never to be any forgiveness, yet this crucifixion is said to have been done by Peter's testimony, by the determined counsel and predetermined plan of God. Why then did God impute to men as a crime what he himself had foreknown, permitted, decreed, and in which, if anywhere, his own finger shone forth? Not unreasonably. For the Father willed the Son to be killed for one purpose; the Devil for another; Judas for a third; and the people for a fourth. Those men, indeed, in order to obey the priests and princes, and the other to gain money, the price of his betrayal; the Devil, in order to remove the Saviour of the world from the midst; but the heavenly Creator, so that through the death of the Only-begotten the redemption of the elect and deliverance from eternal bondage might be obtained. Hear Origen: God delivered up Christ out of mercy toward the human race, since he did not spare his only Son, but delivered him up for us all. The others, however, delivered him up with a wicked purpose, each according to his own malice: Judas out of covetousness, the priests out of envy, the Devil out of fear, lest he should snatch the human race out of his hand through his teaching. Thus Origen distinguishes the manner and end of the divine and human operations in the killing of Christ; but he does not expressly apply and gather this to our purpose, so as to excuse God and accuse man. This Augustine does piously and elegantly, in three different places which agree in sense.

units.la: 16. Ad Vincentium enim sic loquitur: q Cum pater tra-diderit filium suum, & ipse Christus corpus suum, & Iudas Dominum suum, cur in hac traditione, Deus est pius, & homo reus, nisi quia in re-una, quam fecerunt, causa non vna est, ob quam fecerunt: Ita rursus r Si pater filium tradidit, & filius semetipsum tradidit, Iudas quid fe-cit? Pater tradendo filium ad mortem pro nobis, bene fecit; Christus tradendo seipsum pro nobis, fecit bene; tradendo Iudas magistrum pro auaritia, fecit male. Sed & tertio: { In eodem facto, inuenei-nus Deum: Patrem, in quo inuenimus Iudam: Patrem benedicimus, Iudam detestamur. Quare patrem benedicimus, Iudam detestamur? benedicimus charitatem, detestamur iniquitatem. Hactenus Augustinus. Ita, in eodem facto, vt dixi saepius, finis ad quem ferimur, & mo-dus per quem ferimur, diuersum faciunt de rebus iudicium. Si vtrumque horum iustum, & honestum sit; iusta actio futura est: quod si vtrumuis sit malum, in nequitiae scopulos, necesse est vt factum impingat. Cum igitur (vt cunque in la-trinis, & cloacis immunditierum degant homines) purissi-ma omni modo sit Diuina maiestas, cuius oculi in aliis ni-hil perferre immundum possunt, nedum in se, t Sanctitate Domino, & Sanctitate esse Domini clamemus: Creatorem incotaminatum esse, & creaturam lapsam misere, profitea-mur. Diuinam sane in omnibus praesentiam, & incitatione etiam, contemplemur, & admiremur, sed blasphemiam de Deo cogitare vereamur; multo magis lingua proferre. Ca-lumnias Campiani, & hominum malitiosorum, quantum in nobis fuerit, doctrinae sane integritate, & fideli in erudien-do prudentia abstergamus, & amoueamus. Et eousq; ab eo absimus, vt iniustitiā, vel iniquitate, apud Deū esse suspice-mur, & imaginemur, vt n Florinum, & illius sequaces omnes tanquam horrendos Hæreticos, cum antiqua Ecclesia condemnemus: qui malas dixit Deum creasse naturas, atq; substantias: in quantum sunt substantiæ: Cuius dogmatis complexio, & necessaria conclusio, vt peccati authorem, fautoremq; Deum necesse est coarguat. In malam Florinus rem eat, & omnes sui similes, qui, sic, mali Opificem voluerunt esse sanctissimum Creatorem.
units.tr: 16. For to Vincentius he speaks thus: When the Father delivered up his Son, and Christ himself delivered up his body, and Judas his Lord, why in this delivering is God holy and man guilty, unless because in the one deed which they did there is not one cause for which they did it? Again: If the Father delivered up the Son, and the Son delivered up himself, what did Judas do? The Father, in delivering the Son to death for us, did well; Christ, in delivering himself for us, did well; Judas, in delivering the Master for covetousness, did evil. And a third time: In the same deed we find God: we find the Father, in whom we find Judas: we bless the Father, we detest Judas. Why do we bless the Father and detest Judas? We bless the charity, we detest the iniquity. Thus far Augustine. So, in the same deed, as I have said often, the end toward which we are carried and the manner by which we are carried make a different judgment of things. If both of these are just and honourable, the action will be just; but if either is evil, the deed must strike upon the rocks of wickedness. Therefore, since the divine majesty is most pure in every respect (although men live in latrines and sewers of filth), whose eyes can endure nothing unclean in others, much less in themselves, let us proclaim, Holiness to the Lord, and Holiness is the Lord's: let us confess that the Creator is undefiled, and the creature is wretchedly fallen. Let us indeed contemplate and admire the divine presence in all things, and even its incitement, but let us fear to think blasphemy about God, much more to utter it with the tongue. As far as lies in us, let us wipe away and remove by the soundness of doctrine and faithful prudence in teaching the calumnies of Campianus and of wicked men. And let us be so far from him as to suspect and imagine that there is injustice or iniquity with God; and let us condemn Florinus and all his followers, as horrible heretics, together with the ancient Church: who said that God created evil natures and substances, insofar as they are substances. The complexity and necessary conclusion of this doctrine must convict God of being the author and promoter of sin. Let Florinus and all those like him go to their own evil, who wished the most holy Creator to be the author of evil.

units.la: 17. Sicque tandem aliquando, de Mendacio in Rebeccæ fraude: de Baptismo Fœminarū, & Laicorum, in Tipporæ Circūcisione: de Astrologia iudiciaria, in Cantico Deboræ: de præsentia in cultu idololatrico, e facto Naamanis, de fuga Ministri in persecutione, ex discessu Pauli;de integritate, & innocētia Diuina, in sermone hoc Apocalyptico, habetis Lectiones sex. Quas, pro more Academiæ, solennes (si ita loqui liceat) duo fecerunt: vestra præsentia, & attentio, viri doctissimi, grauissimi, sanctissimi, vndiquaq; lectissimi, & rerum ipsarum celebritas. Vtinam & ego is fuissem, qui vel lectione vel ingenio, vel eloquio, vel iudicio, authoritatem etiam potuissem addere. Sed habetis, quales quales fuerint. In quibus discutiendis, illud libentissime profiteor, & agnosco, post immediatā Dei gloriā, & audientiū vtilitatē illum mihi vnicū præfixum fuisse scopum, vt languentium meorum fratrum spiritū excitaré, vt si alicubi (tali potissimū in causa) fit collocanda opera in reb. velint illustriorib. (absit verbo inuidia) illam impendere, iisq; quæ ad vitā cōmunē inprimis faciunt. Digna etenim ea sunt, quæ in tanta Academia, & apud tales viros pertractentur. Multum poterit, in rebus difficilioribus expediendis, varia, multiplexq; lectio, multū poterit industria: plurimum autē animus terrestrib. non affixus, sed sincero Dei cultui deuotus & dicatus. Quod si assiduæ, & frequēti lectioni, si industriæ inuictæ, & indefatigabili, si animo in pietatem consecrato, deuota, humilisq; accesserit oratio, beabit vos Deus, dicamne supra expectationē vestram? imo supra quam cuiquam credibile est: quod ad vestrum modu-lum attinet. Ita, quae ex nostra, qui praecessimus, desunt parte, ex vestra qui sequimini, supplebuntur omnia. Modo, nihil superest, post gratias ex mea parte immortali Deo actas, quin ut Divinum invocemus Spiritum, ut pro inæstimabili sua clementia & misericordia, nobis perpetuo velit affulge-re, ut cum loco Prophetarum, & filiorum Prophetarum sta-tuti simus, ex quorum ore, in corda populi, intelligentia & scientia instillanda sit, sic lucis & veritatis radio, atque face præire velit, ut ea doceamus, quae ad Trinitatis gloriam, ad auditorum fructum, nostramque salutem faciant, in Christo Iesu, cui cum Patre & Spiritu Para-cleto, sit infinitus honor in æternum.
units.tr: 17. And so at last, we have had six lectures: on lying in the deception of Rebecca; on the baptism of women and laymen in the circumcision of Tipporah; on judicial astrology in the Song of Deborah; on the presence at idolatrous worship in the deed of Naaman; on the flight of the minister in persecution, from the departure of Paul; and on the integrity and innocence of God in this Apocalyptic discourse. These, according to the custom of the Academy, two things made solemn (if one may so speak): your presence and attention, most learned, most grave, most holy, most select gentlemen on every side, and the solemnity of the matters themselves. Would that I had been one who could have added authority as well, by reading, by talent, by eloquence or by judgment. But you have them, such as they are. In examining them, I freely profess and acknowledge this: after the immediate glory of God and the usefulness of the hearers, I set before myself this one aim alone, to rouse the spirit of my languishing brethren; so that if anywhere, especially in such a cause, labour ought to be spent on matters of greater weight (let me not say this with envy), I might expend it on those things which above all serve common life. For these are worthy to be treated in so great an Academy and before such men. Varied and manifold reading will count for much in unravelling more difficult matters, and industry will count for much; but most of all a mind not fixed on earthly things, but devoted and dedicated to sincere worship of God. And if devout and humble prayer be added to assiduous and frequent reading, to unconquered and untiring industry, and to a mind consecrated to piety, God will bless you: shall I say beyond your expectation? Indeed, beyond what anyone could believe, as far as your measure goes. Thus whatever is lacking on our part, we who went before, will be fully supplied by yours, who follow. Now nothing remains, after the thanks rendered on my part to the immortal God, but that we invoke the Divine Spirit, that by his inestimable clemency and mercy he may be willing to shine upon us perpetually, so that we may be set in the place of the Prophets and the sons of the Prophets, from whose mouth understanding and knowledge are to be instilled into the hearts of the people; and that he may be willing to go before us with the ray and torch of light and truth, so that we may teach those things which serve the glory of the Trinity, the profit of the hearers, and our own salvation, in Christ Jesus, to whom, with the Father and the Holy Spirit the Paraclete, be infinite honour for ever.
THANKS BE TO GOD.
